info.title: Performativ
info.description:
Welcome to the API documentation for Performativ.

The API is RESTful and designed to be easy to use and understand, with predictable resource-oriented URLs, standard HTTP status codes, and JSON-formatted responses.

tags.name: Advice
tags.description:
Advice policies define the business rules governing an advice context's behavior. A policy is assigned when creating an advice context and controls which transitions and actions are permitted.

**Available policies:**

| Policy                         | Behavior                                                                                                                                                                          |
|--------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `default`                      | Permissive. Agreements not required for sessions. Signing envelope not required before submit-signing.                                                                             |
| `advisory_control_lifecycle`   | Strict. Agreements required before sessions. Signed agreement needed to activate a session. Member changes auto-revoke agreements. Signing envelope must be linked before submit-signing. |

Policies are read-only configuration — list and show only.

tags.name: Intentions
tags.description:
Intentions are transient coordination records for cross-system operations. They represent "I want to do X with Y — the resolver acknowledges, does the work, and reports the result."

**Use cases:**
- Launching a third-party tool with synced data
- Preparing a trade intent for review
- Any operation requiring external system readiness before proceeding

**Lifecycle:**

    pending ──┬─► in_progress ─┬─► succeeded
              │                ├─► failed
              ├─► succeeded    └─► cancelled / expired
              ├─► failed
              └─► cancelled / expired

Inline resolvers may transition pending → succeeded/failed directly. The
in_progress hop is optional and exists for resolvers that want to expose a
working state to the consumer (progress updates, long-running work).

**Flow:**
1. UI creates intention (targeted or broadcast)
2. Plugin receives webhook, optionally marks in_progress, then marks complete with result payload
3. UI polls for succeeded status, then acts on result (e.g., redirect)
4. Intentions auto-expire after TTL (default 5 minutes)

For broadcast intentions (no resolver assigned at create time), the first
resolver to call any state-changing endpoint atomically claims ownership.
Subsequent resolvers receive 409. Two plugins cannot share an intention.

tags.name: Documents & Reports
tags.description:
Documents store files (PDFs, images, etc.) uploaded via S3 presigned URLs or direct upload. They serve multiple purposes across the platform — client files, reports, contracts, and advisory agreement documents.

**Key document types for the advice domain:**

| Type                         | Purpose                                                                        |
|------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `advisory_agreement`         | Unsigned agreement document                                                    |
| `advisory_agreement_signed`  | Signed agreement document (conventional type, not enforced by `mark-signed`)   |

Documents can be referenced by ID in advisory agreement actions (e.g. `signed_document_id` in `mark-signed`). The `signed_document_id` is optional — under strict policy, the signing envelope's documents are checked instead.

tags.name: Fees & Billing
tags.description: Endpoints for managing fee definitions, fee sets, fee coverage assignments, invoices, and invoice batches. Fee definitions are tenant-wide templates that define calculation rules; fee coverage links them to specific clients or portfolios. Invoice batches group generated invoices for review and approval.

tags.name: Search
tags.description: Cross-entity omnibar search endpoint. Searches across clients, persons, portfolios, cash accounts, instruments, and groups using FULLTEXT indexing with ACL-scoped filtering. Results are ranked by relevance and can be narrowed by entity type.

tags.name: Me
tags.description: Endpoints scoped to the authenticated user. Retrieve and update your own profile, permissions, context (clients, groups, segments), MFA settings, and security configuration without needing a user ID.

tags.name: Users & Access
tags.description: Endpoints for managing platform users, roles, permissions, advisors, personal access tokens, and onboarding links. Users are globally scoped (not client-owned). Role assignments control permission grants, and advisors link users to client relationships.

tags.name: Clients
tags.description: Endpoints for managing clients and their related data: persons, credentials, external IDs, questionnaires, businesses, group tags, user categories, and client activity logs. Clients are the primary ownership entity for portfolios, transactions, and most scoped resources.

tags.name: Metrics
tags.description: Read-only computed financial metrics for clients, portfolios, and cash accounts. Includes time-series performance (TWR, MWR, PnL), snapshots, holdings breakdowns, allocation trees, AUM aggregates, and entity-level risk metrics. Data is computed on-demand by the valuation microservice.

tags.name: Persons
tags.description: Endpoints for managing persons (natural individuals) and their related data: addresses, external IDs, relationship types, and person-to-person relationships. Persons are linked to clients through client-person associations and can have multiple relationship types (e.g. spouse, child, power of attorney).

tags.name: Configuration
tags.description: Endpoints for tenant-wide platform configuration: platform settings, organizational units, account categories, custom field definitions, custom field values, custom actions, and setting configurations. These resources control system behavior, define custom data models, and configure tenant-specific business rules.

tags.name: Groups & Segments
tags.description: Endpoints for managing client groups, segments, segment types, tags, and segment-client assignments. Groups are user-defined collections of clients; segments are rule-based partitions used for access control, reporting, and configuration overlays. Tags provide lightweight labeling for clients within groups.

tags.name: Instruments
tags.description: Endpoints for managing financial instruments and their related data: prices, costs, benchmarks, composite benchmarks, exchanges, handlers, instrument types, fixed income details, derivatives, private equity cash flows, corporate actions, market data, and instrument search. Instruments represent tradeable securities, funds, and other financial products held in portfolios.

tags.name: Portfolios
tags.description: Endpoints for managing portfolios and their related data: positions, cash accounts, cash account types, cash account movement categories, portfolio types, funding accounts, commitments, savings plans, expected cash flows, tradable instruments, and computed portfolio values. Portfolios belong to clients and hold instrument positions and cash accounts.

tags.name: Transactions
tags.description: Endpoints for managing transactions and related data: transaction types, transaction import mappings, cash movements, cash transfers, external balances, external positions, and duplicate detection. Transactions record buy/sell/transfer activity against portfolios; cash movements track deposits, withdrawals, and fee debits on cash accounts.

tags.name: Reference Data
tags.description: Endpoints for managing shared reference data: currencies, countries, regions, languages, sectors, and industries. These are tenant-wide lookup tables used across instruments, clients, and portfolios. Globally scoped with no client-level access control.

tags.name: Allocations
tags.description: Endpoints for managing allocation breakdowns on instruments: dimensions, dimension values, allocations, and allocation items. Allocations define how an instrument's weight is distributed across dimension values (e.g. geography, sector, asset class). Versioned — each update creates a new allocation version.

tags.name: Risk
tags.description: Endpoints for managing risk profiles, risk metrics (Monte Carlo simulations), and stress scenarios. Risk profiles are global reference data assigned to clients and portfolios; risk metrics provide on-demand simulation results from the valuation microservice.

tags.name: Rules & Compliance
tags.description: Endpoints for managing compliance rules, rule sets, rule-model portfolio assignments, rule coverage, and data transformation rules. Rules define screening, monitoring, and trading constraints that are evaluated against client portfolios. Rule coverage links rules to specific clients or segments.

tags.name: Dashboards
tags.description: Endpoints for managing dashboard layouts, dashboard widgets, table widgets, and expression definitions. Dashboard layouts store per-page tab and widget configurations; widgets define the content rendered in each layout slot. Layouts are tenant-wide and support named layout variants per page.

tags.name: Alerts
tags.description: Endpoints for viewing alerts, alert instances, and alert suppressions. Alerts are generated internally by scanner jobs and compliance rules; the V1 API exposes them read-only. Alert suppressions allow dismissing or snoozing specific alerts. Alert instances track per-entity occurrences of alert definitions.

tags.name: Integrations
tags.description: Endpoints for managing plugins, plugin instances, webhook deliveries, bulk import (sync and async), and bulk import templates. Plugins represent external integrations; plugin instances are tenant-specific activations with configuration and webhook subscriptions. Bulk import provides CSV-based data loading with dependency-ordered processing.

tags.name: Activity & History
tags.description: Endpoints for viewing audit trails and status change history. Activity logs record every create, update, and delete event on tenant entities, filterable by entity type, event, causer, and date range. Status history tracks lifecycle state transitions for entities with status workflows.
